test_title: SSC CHSL Exam 2023 Tier-II Official Paper (Held On: 10 Jan, 2024 Shift 1).
subject: general
question: What is 'Phishing' in the context of network security?

options.text: A type of computer worm that spreads through email attachments.
An attack that floods a network with excessive traffic to disrupt its operation.
A social engineering attack that tricks users into revealing sensitive information.
A type of malware that spreads through infected USB drives.

solution:
The correct answer is __**3) A social engineering attack that tricks users into revealing sensitive information.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Phishing** is a type of social engineering attack often used to steal user data, including login credentials and credit card numbers.
 
• It occurs when an attacker, masquerading as a trusted entity, dupes a victim into opening an email, instant message, or text message.
 
• The recipient is then tricked into clicking a malicious link, which can lead to the installation of malware, the freezing of the system as part of a ransomware attack, or the revealing of sensitive information.
 
• Phishing is one of the oldest and most widespread internet scams, and it continues to be a significant concern in network security.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Phishing attacks** can be conducted through various communication channels including email, social media, phone calls, and text messages.
 
• Common signs of phishing attempts include unsolicited requests for sensitive information, generic greetings, and suspicious links or attachments.
 
• To protect against phishing, users should verify the source of unexpected requests, use multi-factor authentication, and keep their software updated.
 
• Organizations often conduct **phishing awareness training** to educate employees about recognizing and responding to phishing attempts.
 
• Reporting phishing attempts to appropriate authorities can help in mitigating the risks and preventing future attacks.
